summaryZh: 美国众议员Zach Nunn（共和党-爱荷华州）和Don Davis（民主党-北卡罗来纳州）联合提出《FARM AI法案》，旨在通过将人工智能纳入美国农业部优先研究领域、扩展推广服务、增加农村劳动力培训资助以及设立AI顾问职位，加速AI在农业中的部署。法案针对农场采用AI面临的高成本、技术短缺等挑战，强调从实验室到田间的转化，对智慧畜牧和精准农业具有重要政策导向意义。
featuredReason: 该法案直接针对AI在农业（包括养殖业）落地中的资金、培训、标准等核心痛点，为智慧畜牧从业者提供了政策风向标和潜在资源对接机会，值得关注后续进展。

Bipartisan bill introduced to incorporate AI into farms

Gianna Willcox

WASHINGTON — U.S. Reps. Zach Nunn (R-Iowa) and Don Davis (D-N.C.) recently introduced a bipartisan bill to facilitate the deployment of artificial intelligence across American agriculture by modernizing USDA research and workforce programs.

The act is the Fostering Agricultural Research and Modernization through Artificial Intelligent Act, or FARM AI Act for short.

The FARM AI Act will:

Designate artificial intelligence as a priority research area under USDA’s Agriculture and Food Research Initiative (AFRI) and expand AI research through the Agriculture Advanced Research and Development Authority (AgRDA).

Equip USDA Extension with the resources to help farmers responsibly adopt AI technologies and precision agriculture.

Expand USDA grants and fellowships to strengthen the rural workforce and prepare the next generation of agricultural innovators.

Nominate a senior USDA official as the AI in Agriculture Advisor to coordinate federal AI efforts, align agency programs, and work with the National Institute of Standards and Technology to develop national standards for agricultural AI.

“Iowa farmers have always been the first to put new technology to work when it helps them grow more efficiently, conserve resources, and stay competitive. Artificial intelligence is the next frontier,” Rep. Nunn said in a statement. “From yield mapping and precision nutrient application to disease detection and water conservation, AI gives farmers better information to make better decisions in real time. Our bipartisan FARM AI Act builds on the groundbreaking research already happening at Iowa’s universities while investing in the workforce needed to bring these innovations from the lab to the field. The future of agriculture shouldn’t be written by bureaucrats in Washington — it should be driven by the Iowa farmers who feed America.”

Iowa State University is already working on bringing AI to the forefront of agriculture and farms. The AI Institute for Resilient Agriculture, based at ISU and supported by the National Science Foundation and USDA’s National Food and Agriculture, is developing AI-powered models of crops and entire farming systems to help breeders develop stronger varieties and help producers improve yields while using fewer resources, Nunn’s bill announcement stated.

In addition to developing AI tools, ISU is also leading innovation across the Midwest. On July 14, the NSF announced that ISU will lead a network that brings together community colleges, industry partners, entrepreneurs, and investors to accelerate innovation in the bioeconomy.

However, despite the rapid advancement of research, farmers and producers are still facing major problems when trying to put these AI tools to work. High upfront costs, limited technical expertise, and a shortage of rural workforce training have slowed adoption of AI technologies on many farms, the announcement noted.

The FARM AI Act addresses all of these challenges.

“Feeding America is national security, and the future of agriculture will depend on our ability to innovate,” Rep. Davis said. “We must strengthen research, expand workforce training, and give producers the tools they need to increase productivity, remain globally competitive, and ensure the United States continues to lead the world in agriculture.”

The FARM AI Act is the House companion to bipartisan legislation introduced in the Senate by Senators Ted Budd (R-N.C.) and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), the announcement added.

The full text of the bill can be found here.

translationZh:
华盛顿——美国众议员Zach Nunn（共和党-爱荷华州）和Don Davis（民主党-北卡罗来纳州）近日提出了一项两党法案，旨在通过现代化美国农业部的研究和劳动力计划，推动人工智能在美国农业中的部署。

该法案全称为《通过人工智能促进农业研究和现代化法案》，简称FARM AI法案。

**FARM AI法案将：**

将人工智能指定为美国农业部农业与食品研究倡议下的优先研究领域，并通过农业高级研究与发展管理局扩大AI研究。

为美国农业部推广服务提供资源，帮助农民负责任地采用AI技术和精准农业。

扩大美国农业部的资助和奖学金，以加强农村劳动力，培养下一代农业创新者。

任命一名美国农业部高级官员担任农业AI顾问，协调联邦AI工作，协调各机构项目，并与国家标准与技术研究院合作制定农业AI国家标准。

“爱荷华州的农民一直是率先使用新技术的群体，这些技术帮助他们更高效地种植、节约资源并保持竞争力。人工智能是下一个前沿领域，”Nunn议员在一份声明中表示。“从产量绘图和精准养分施用，到疾病检测和水资源保护，AI为农民提供更好的信息，使他们能够实时做出更明智的决策。我们的两党FARM AI法案建立在爱荷华州大学已经开展的突破性研究基础上，同时投资于将这些创新从实验室带到田间所需的人才队伍。农业的未来不应由华盛顿的官僚决定——而应由养活美国的爱荷华州农民来推动。”

爱荷华州立大学已经在将AI推向农业和农场的前沿。Nunn议员的法案公告指出，由爱荷华州立大学主导、美国国家科学基金会和美国农业部国家食品与农业研究所支持的韧性农业AI研究所，正在开发基于AI的作物和整个农业系统模型，以帮助育种者培育更强壮的品种，并帮助生产者用更少的资源提高产量。

除了开发AI工具，爱荷华州立大学还在引领中西部地区的创新。7月14日，美国国家科学基金会宣布，爱荷华州立大学将领导一个网络，汇聚社区学院、行业合作伙伴、企业家和投资者，以加速生物经济领域的创新。

然而，尽管研究进展迅速，农民和生产者在尝试将这些AI工具投入实际应用时仍面临重大障碍。公告指出，高昂的前期成本、有限的技术专长以及农村劳动力培训的短缺，减缓了AI技术在许多农场的采用。

FARM AI法案旨在应对所有这些挑战。

“养活美国是国家安全问题，农业的未来将取决于我们创新的能力，”Davis议员表示。“我们必须加强研究，扩大劳动力培训，为生产者提供提高生产力、保持全球竞争力所需的工具，并确保美国继续在农业领域引领世界。”

公告补充说，FARM AI法案是参议员Ted Budd（共和党-北卡罗来纳州）和Adam Schiff（民主党-加利福尼亚州）在参议院提出的两党立法的众议院配套法案。

法案全文可在此处查阅。
